title: AI agent vs chatbot: what you are handing over
h1: ai agent vs chatbot: answers, actions and responsibility
description: A plain comparison of asking for an answer and handing over a task, with permission boundaries and a way to decide how much help you need.
answer: **a chatbot tells you how to rename files. an agent renames them.** the difference is who takes the next step. for a paragraph rewrite, a conversation may be all you need. for a friday folder review, you need file access and a schedule. look at the tools and permissions behind the name before handing over the job.
og_line: decide what you want to hand over.

them: **keep the next step yours.** you want an explanation, second opinion or draft.
**act after reading.** you prefer to carry out each change yourself.
dusk: **hand over a small job.** it needs to read allowed material and use tools.
**repeat work with clear limits.** you can define access, stopping rules and review.

compare.h: a working distinction, not two fixed product categories
compare.intro: **the next step is the useful dividing line.** a product can offer both conversation and action. dusk illustrates the agent column; other agents have different tools and controls.

rows.label: what you hand over
cells: a question, passage or idea to discuss
a job, allowed inputs and a clear place for the result

rows.label: who takes the next step
cells: you read the answer and do the next action
the agent may call permitted tools and continue the task

rows.label: access to other apps
cells: for a conversation-only task, you supply the material
may read connected apps or change them, depending on permissions

rows.label: when work starts
cells: you start this exchange by asking
may start in chat, on a schedule or from an app event

rows.label: checking progress
cells: you inspect the reply before using it
in Metal, tool activity is shown while the bot works; you can stop it

rows.label: memory and identity
cells: a conversation interface alone says nothing about lasting memory
dusk bots have separate jobs and memory; memory can be turned off

method:
**the labels describe responsibility, not a ranking.** we make Metal and use its docs for the agent examples.

we didn't run matching tests across products. a chat interface can include tools, memory and background work. inspect the controls before deciding how much authority a product gets.

sections.md:
**a paragraph rewrite can stay a conversation.** paste the passage, discuss it and take the next step yourself. explanations, second opinions and draft wording often need no app access.

try: "which terms in this paragraph are unclear? ask what i mean before rewriting it." you get help thinking and keep the original intact.

the [agent explainer](/guides/what-is-an-ai-agent) covers the vocabulary. choose around the work you need done.

**an agent helps when the result needs more than a reply.** a friday folder review needs file access and a schedule. dusk routines start through chat and show their next runs on a card.[^4]

try: "every friday at 3, read this project folder's notes. list unanswered questions here. change nothing. stay quiet if there are none." [scheduled tasks](/scheduled-ai-tasks) turns a repeated request into work to supervise.

the machine still matters. dusk desktop routines stop during sleep or when the app closes. dusk cloud runs them on time.[^4]

**use a fixed rule when a fixed rule will do.** if the same input always needs the same action, spell out the process. messy notes may need judgement; tell the agent which evidence to use.

in dusk, read-only app access blocks changes. other app edits can happen without asking, so require confirmation before allowing writes.[^3] file and command approvals are separate.[^6]

watch the first runs and stop if the job grows. the [computer-control safety guide](/guides/is-it-safe-to-let-ai-control-your-computer) helps you choose its limits.

faq.q: what are the best uses for an agent in personal life?
faq.a: **start with a review you can read against the original.** name the notes or folder, result destination and quiet rule. keep changes out of the first routine.

faq.q: does a chatbot become an agent just because it remembers me?
faq.a: **memory is separate from action.** dusk has a memory setting and app permissions for tools.[^5][^3] ask what it can do on your behalf, not just what it recalls.

faq.q: do i need a group chat of agents for a simple job?
faq.a: **start with one bot.** dusk supports small, focused groups.[^7] add another job when it brings a distinct contribution.

steps: choose a paragraph you want help with
ask for suggestions without changing the original
write down any next step you still do yourself
consider an agent only when that step needs tools

rows: explain or rewrite material you paste
an agent with read access and a schedule
apply the same fixed rule every time
make a decision with missing evidence
a person who can resolve the gaps

mistakes.mistake: granting an account for a small question
mistakes.fix: paste the relevant excerpt when that is enough.

mistakes.mistake: assuming an agent runs all night
mistakes.fix: find where it runs. a local routine stops with the computer or app.

tip.text: ask what the software can change. that answer tells you more than the word agent on its homepage.
